question:
An 8-year-old male comes for a routine pediatric check-up. He is socially well-adjusted, participates in
chess club, and enjoys gaming. His past medical history includes asthma managed with albuterol.
Physical examination reveals: weight at 99th percentile, height at 30th percentile, BMI 39.1 kg/m^2,
temperature 97.3°F (37.5°C), blood pressure 115/89 mmHg, heart rate 90/min, respiratory rate 8/min,
and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. The patient is engaged and maintains appropriate eye contact.
Cardiac, pulmonary, abdominal, neurological, and musculoskeletal examinations are unremarkable.
What is the most probable health outcome for this patient in the next decade? Answer Choices: (A)
Metabolic syndrome (B) Left ventricular hypertrophy (C) Precocious puberty (D) Constitutional growth
delay (E) Slipped capital femoral epiphysis (F) Obstructive sleep apnea (G) Type 2 diabetes mellitus

(H) Early-onset osteoarthritis (I) Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (J) Renovascular hypertension
 A. Renovascular hypertension
B. Left ventricular hypertrophy
C. Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
D. Constitutional growth delay
E. Metabolic syndrome
F. Precocious puberty
G. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
H. Early-onset osteoarthritis
I. Obstructive sleep apnea
J. Slipped capital femoral epiphysis
